settings.title: Worldwide Contact System
settings.strapline: Connect people and practical work across places and cultures.

pages.heading: Find a route into every place.
pages.body: A contact workbench for GAJRA Earth, P4A and the Web3 Sensorium. Explore existing networks, connect useful work to local needs and prepare a relevant introduction.

pages.heading: Start with an existing connection.
pages.body: Find public directories and organisations that can open a conversation. Check the local organisation and choose the appropriate contact route.

pages.heading: Every place has its own context.
pages.body: Explore the country and territory reference list. Record real connections as they develop, while making room for communities that cross borders.

pages.heading: Useful work gives an invitation substance.
pages.body: Approach people through a subject that matters locally. These connected projects offer several ways to begin.

pages.heading: Prepare a relevant introduction.
pages.body: Choose the place, project and request. Make the wording your own, then decide how to share it.

pages.heading: Make contact. Keep the next step clear.
pages.body: A repeatable way to find appropriate people, make a useful approach and turn replies into direct relationships.

pages.heading: Keep the working records together.
pages.body: Edit public website content in the CMS. Keep personal contacts, correspondence and outreach decisions in the private workspace.

projects.title: Your Relevance in every jurisdiction
projects.summary: Adapt the method of investigating the rules affecting a person's own circumstances to the sources, jurisdictions and choices relevant in each place.
projects.invite: Discuss a locally grounded adaptation of Your Relevance, or introduce people interested in legal understanding and informed civic participation.

projects.title: Australian Legal Engine
projects.summary: Retrieve and quote provisions from locally indexed Australian legislation, with source addresses and dates. Follow connections between acts and bring the original text into a legal research conversation.
projects.invite: Discuss source-grounded legal research, locally held legislation and ways to make relevant provisions easier to find and check.

projects.title: Installing the Missing Middle
projects.summary: Develop community-scale computing with useful heat, resilient power, workforce learning and a pathway to local ownership. Personal and community data authority remains part of the design.
projects.invite: Explore a place-specific conversation about community computing, locally useful workloads, installation capability and data authority.

projects.title: P4A Australia
projects.summary: Explore civic participation through local places, everyday issues, public evidence and connected proposals for Australia's future.
projects.invite: Discuss relevant local civic or cultural questions, suggest a source, or introduce interested residents and community organisations.

projects.title: P4A Oceania
projects.summary: Explore how P4A's civic workbench could translate across Oceania, with local contexts, regional connections and questions shaped by the people who live there.
projects.invite: Introduce interested residents or local organisations to discuss civic participation, regional connections and locally relevant ideas across Oceania.

projects.title: P4A Native Nations
projects.summary: Explore Indigenous nations, treaties, knowledge and data sovereignty, with participation and locally chosen pathways grounded in each nation's own authority.
projects.invite: Discuss an appropriate introduction or locally chosen contribution, with the relevant Indigenous people determining the scope and sharing of their knowledge.

projects.title: GAJRA Earth Infinity
projects.summary: A public presentation of Joyful Responsible Abundance as living practice, with local interpretation, reflection, contribution and connections across cultures.
projects.invite: Connect with Luke about locally meaningful participation, language and cultural perspectives, or practical work that people choose to develop together.

projects.title: GAJRA Earth Claude
projects.summary: Explore the Claude-built GAJRA Earth invitation: Joyful Responsible Abundance, human and AI alignment, and questions people can help define across cultures.
projects.invite: Invite a conversation about Joyful Responsible Abundance, public questions and locally meaningful contributions to human and AI alignment.

projects.title: GAJRA Earth Community
projects.summary: Find starting points for shared action through GAJRA Earth's public hub: community contributions, events, travel, research and practical work towards Joyful Responsible Abundance.
projects.invite: Introduce a local interest, useful skill or community project and explore how people might contribute and share what they learn.

projects.title: Aura Genesis
projects.summary: Explore the Aura Genesis Protocol: developing personal intelligence through a digital twin of body and mind, reflective learning and the proposed Genesis process.
projects.invite: Discuss personal intelligence, reflective learning and a locally relevant starting point for exploring the Aura Genesis proposal.

projects.title: Aura Tourism
projects.summary: Explore personal intelligence through travel, music, sport, culture, nature and reflection, beginning on Minjerribah and connecting with wider tourism and learning opportunities.
projects.invite: Discuss a tourism or community learning opportunity that connects enjoyable experiences, local knowledge and personal intelligence.

projects.title: Aura Disaster Resilience
projects.summary: Connect everyday community capability with location-specific preparedness, communications, practical learning and continuing recovery.
projects.invite: Discuss local hazards, community knowledge and practical preparedness or recovery work, and identify interested local contributors.

projects.title: Aura Children & Young People
projects.summary: Explore a proposal for children and young people in Australian care, beginning with chosen interests and supported creative learning. Connect self-understanding, rights, family, culture and mentoring with opportunities for adulthood.
projects.invite: Discuss supported creative learning, mentoring or a locally relevant introduction for exploring the children and young people's Aura proposal.

projects.title: Aura Whole-of-Life Support
projects.summary: Explore proposed personal-intelligence support for adults living with dementia or disability, people beginning aged care and their supporters. Connect memory, personal context and everyday choices with human-directed support.
projects.invite: Discuss an everyday support need, a potential research or service partnership, or an introduction to supporters interested in the whole-of-life proposal.

projects.title: Verse Box
projects.summary: Explore a proposed portable introduction to Aura of Intelligence: personal Aura building, learning, Community Hours and civic participation using lower-cost equipment.
projects.invite: Explore a locally useful public demonstration, a possible host setting or a contribution to personal Aura learning and community participation.

projects.title: A fair go in the age of intelligence
projects.summary: Luke's UNGA81 contribution invites locally shaped cooperation around Joyful Responsible Abundance, meaningful choices and useful capability shared between places.
projects.invite: Circulate the invitation or discuss how locally rooted associations could cooperate across countries and cultures while retaining their own judgment.

projects.title: Joyful Responsible Abundance
projects.summary: Explore how personal intelligence, community capability, sovereign compute and civic participation connect in a whole-system proposal for Joyful Responsible Abundance, with source papers and tools for considering Australian choices in the age of superintelligence.
projects.invite: Discuss a locally meaningful starting point for Joyful Responsible Abundance, or connect a community interest with the proposal's practical tools and source papers.

projects.title: Mutual Futures
projects.summary: Explore shared ownership, business succession, learning, care and time through the AI transition. Connect productive technology with local capability, livelihoods and opportunities people can help shape.
projects.invite: Introduce a business handover, community need, useful skill or shared-ownership idea and explore a practical contribution to Mutual Futures.

sources.name: Grassroots Justice Network
sources.summary: An organisation directory for discovering legal empowerment groups. Listings are crowdsourced and require verification.
sources.contact_route: Use the organisation listing to identify its own public website or appropriate organisational enquiry route. Do not harvest member personal details.

sources.name: GNDR
sources.summary: A directory of civil society organisations working on disaster reduction and community resilience, with routes to national focal points.
sources.contact_route: Find an organisation or national focal point, verify its current public contact route, then enquire about an introduction or appropriate circulation.

sources.name: Association for Progressive Communications
sources.summary: A network of organisations working on community technology, communications, digital rights and local capability.
sources.contact_route: Follow the Members route from APC's own site and approach a relevant organisation through its published contact channel.

sources.name: Internet Society chapters
sources.summary: A chapter directory with public websites and contact emails for local Internet-related work.
sources.contact_route: Choose the relevant chapter, check its website and published organisational contact, and ask about community technology connections.

sources.name: Asia Indigenous Peoples Pact
sources.summary: A regional network of Indigenous peoples' organisations. Its own public site provides a route to the regional organisation.
sources.contact_route: Ask the regional organisation or an identified member's own public contact how to make a relevant invitation available.

sources.name: Indigenous Peoples of Africa Co-ordinating Committee
sources.summary: An African network of Indigenous peoples' organisations with a public member-organisation map.
sources.contact_route: Use the member map or published regional contact to identify an appropriate organisational introduction.

sources.name: Global Voices and Rising Voices
sources.summary: Public routes into a community of writers, translators and participatory media practitioners, including work with underrepresented language communities.
sources.contact_route: Follow contributor, Rising Voices or partnership routes and approach the appropriate published organisational contact.

sources.name: Wikimedia affiliates and user groups
sources.summary: A directory of geographic, thematic and language-related affiliates, including groups with established contact people.
sources.contact_route: Read the relevant group page and use its stated contact or discussion channel for a suitable introduction.

sources.name: URI Cooperation Circles
sources.summary: A searchable directory of community-led groups working across cultures, faiths and traditions.
sources.contact_route: Search by region, country or subject, read the group's own description, and use its published contact route.

sources.name: WFUNA national associations
sources.summary: A public directory of national United Nations Associations and organisational contact routes.
sources.contact_route: Identify a relevant national association and approach its published office contact about circulation or a conversation.

sources.name: Rotary and Rotaract clubs
sources.summary: An entry route to service clubs, local organisers and the connected Rotary and Rotaract networks.
sources.contact_route: Use the club-finding routes and a club's own public contact details to ask about an appropriate introduction or circulation.

sources.name: Toastmasters club finder
sources.summary: A club finder with routes to message club officers and identify meetings suitable for English communication.
sources.contact_route: Select a relevant open club, confirm its meeting language, and enquire through its listed officer-contact route.

sources.name: Servas groups
sources.summary: A directory of national and regional Servas group websites and social pages where provided.
sources.contact_route: Use the relevant group's own published contact route to enquire about English-speaking residents and suitable introductions.

sources.name: TESOL affiliate associations
sources.summary: An affiliate directory connecting national and regional English-language teaching associations.
sources.contact_route: Follow an association's own website and contact its organising committee about a relevant invitation or introduction.

sources.name: IATEFL teaching associations
sources.summary: An entry route to national and regional teaching associations within IATEFL's associate network.
sources.contact_route: Identify the appropriate association, verify its own contact details and ask about a relevant circulation or introduction.

sources.name: Co-operative and local trade networks
sources.summary: Use the ICA member directory as one research route to co-operative organisations. Find local trade and professional groups separately for the particular place.
sources.contact_route: Identify a relevant organisation, verify its own public contact and local relevance, and ask about community capability or practical introductions.

sources.name: CREATE Foundation
sources.summary: National peak body for children and young people with out-of-home-care experience, with youth advisory and participation programs. Suggested approach: A strong first approach for learning how care-experienced young people could shape supported creative learning, interests and transition-to-adulthood proposals.
sources.contact_route: Email the published national office at create@create.org.au with a concise organisational partnership enquiry. The contact page explicitly welcomes discussion about partnering; ask which program or state team should review the proposal. Note: CREATE describes its role as systemic advocacy rather than casework or individual care decisions. An organisational enquiry does not grant access to young people or imply willingness to trial a product.

sources.name: SNAICC – National Voice for our Children
sources.summary: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander community-controlled peak body for children, young people and families, with early childhood and child-and-family sector work. Suggested approach: A route for asking how a children-and-learning proposal could be discussed with appropriate community-controlled organisations and grounded in family, culture and community priorities.
sources.contact_route: Use info@snaicc.org.au or the official contact form for a general or sector-related enquiry. Describe the proposal and request direction to the appropriate team or community-controlled route; training@snaicc.org.au is specifically for training enquiries. Note: National sector engagement is not permission to represent a particular Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander nation, share community knowledge or work with local children. Local organisations determine their involvement.

sources.name: FICE International – International Federation of Educative Communities
sources.summary: International network of national sections, organisations and professionals working with children and young people, including those in out-of-home care. Suggested approach: A practical international route for discussing supported creative learning and exchanging care-and-education practice with relevant national sections.
sources.contact_route: Start with the published international secretariat email fice.inter@gmail.com or its organisational contact form. Ask for the relevant national-section introduction; use the official country member list to identify possible follow-up organisations. Note: The official country member list is a discovery route, not evidence of worldwide coverage. Individual national contact details and external destinations have not all been revalidated; confirm them through the secretariat before follow-up.

sources.name: Alzheimer's Disease International (ADI)
sources.summary: Federation of national Alzheimer associations, with a public country-filtered member directory and links to association profiles. Suggested approach: An efficient country-by-country discovery route for relevant dementia organisations when exploring personal-context support, accessible demonstrations and local collaboration.
sources.contact_route: Select a country in the official member directory, open the association's profile, then check its official organisational contact channel. ADI's own contact page also distinguishes questions about its work from individual support requests. Note: Directory membership is not universal country coverage, proof of a local participant or permission to contact people receiving services. Use organisational collaboration channels rather than national support helplines; individual member routes require their own check.

sources.name: Dementia Alliance International (DAI)
sources.summary: An organisation of people with dementia, with international self-advocacy, human-rights work and an organisational contact form. Suggested approach: A lived-experience-led route for asking whether and how people with dementia would want to help shape personal-context technology and everyday support proposals.
sources.contact_route: Use the official Contact Us form for an organisational collaboration enquiry. Explain the proposed support use and ask about an appropriate way to discuss it; the sponsor/partner page is a separate route for sponsorship interest. Note: DAI membership is for people medically diagnosed with dementia or mild cognitive impairment. An external project proposer should use the organisational form rather than join as a member or approach peer-support groups to pitch. International eligibility does not establish participation in every country.

sources.name: Dementia Australia – product development and research collaboration
sources.summary: Dedicated channels for discussing technology development, potential co-development, research collaboration and involvement of Dementia Advocates. Suggested approach: The clearest specific Australian route for reviewing a dementia-related personal-intelligence proposal and exploring suitable co-design or evaluation.
sources.contact_route: Use the Product support form for the technology proposal. For a defined research project, use the Research Collaboration Request form or research@dementia.org.au. For lived-experience input, use Work with a Dementia Advocate or advocates@dementia.org.au. These are organisational channels, separate from the support helpline. Note: Dementia Australia explicitly excludes product endorsement, third-party product promotion and financial investment. Assistance depends on capacity; fees may apply and advocate participation is voluntary. Its product co-development terms may require ownership of some or all resulting intellectual property. Research recruitment-only requests follow a separate study-listing route.

sources.name: People with Disability Australia (PWDA) – research and consultancy
sources.summary: Disability-led research and consultancy services, including advisory participation, inclusive research, focus groups and program-development advice. Suggested approach: A direct organisational route for disability-led design of support, accessible personal technology, legal-information access and preparedness proposals.
sources.contact_route: Email pwd@pwd.org.au, the address explicitly published for research partnerships and consultancy. Specify a research or consultancy enquiry and the advice sought; use this route rather than the individual-advocacy intake form. Note: Consultancy is fee-for-service. Research expectations include co-creation, contribution recognition, remuneration, accessible materials and the ability to withdraw. PWDA says it will not consider partnership proposals within one month of an application deadline. An enquiry does not secure participants or a partnership.

sources.name: Australian Rehabilitation & Assistive Technology Association (ARATA)
sources.summary: Assistive-technology association with a public practitioner directory covering expert technology users, allied health professionals, educators, advisers and suppliers. Suggested approach: A practical route to relevant technical and accessibility expertise for everyday support, creative-learning access and portable demonstrations across age groups.
sources.contact_route: Search the official practitioner directory by locality, profession and age-group experience to identify relevant professional services. For association-level introductions or an initial project discussion, use office@arata.org.au, published on its Contact Us page. Note: The directory concerns professional expertise and services; listings are maintained by members. It is not a list of willing research participants or an endorsement of this project. Individual availability, current details and any professional fees require follow-up.

sources.name: Assistive Technology Suppliers Australia (ATSA)
sources.summary: Assistive-technology supplier industry body with a public member directory, product categories and community-accessible industry events. Suggested approach: Useful for identifying equipment and accessibility providers, or asking about appropriate demonstration and supplier-development settings for Verse Box and support technology.
sources.contact_route: Use the member directory to identify relevant businesses, including communication aids, electronic devices and home automation. For an association-level enquiry use info@atsa.org.au or the official Contact ATSA form; ask about the appropriate supplier or event route. Note: ATSA is an industry and supplier route rather than a substitute for disability-led co-design. Supplier listings do not establish research interest, accessible suitability, funding or product endorsement. Commercial and event participation terms need separate discussion.

sources.name: Pacific Islands Association of Non-Governmental Organisations (PIANGO)
sources.summary: Pacific civil-society umbrella network with an official country-by-country directory of national NGO coordinating bodies. A practical route to locally relevant community organisations for P4A Oceania and GAJRA. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: national umbrella routes can put a specific local civic or community proposal before organisations already working in the relevant place.
sources.contact_route: Choose a relevant National Liaison Unit in the official member directory, follow its organisational website/contact, and request one suitable local introduction or consideration of a short invitation for circulation. Note: Directory inclusion does not establish present officer details, independence or interest. Confirm the selected organisation's current contact on its own site before sending; no blanket circulation or country coverage is assumed.

sources.name: Pacific Disability Forum
sources.summary: Regional disability network offering an official member directory and a public organisational enquiry route. Relevant to accessible participation, whole-of-life tools and visitor experiences. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: it offers a relevant route for asking whether accessibility and participant-directed uses of the additional Aura and Verse Box projects merit a local discussion.
sources.contact_route: Use its contact form or published general email infor@pacificdisability.org; ask for the appropriate membership or country-organisation route. Consult the member directory for a specific place. Note: No clinical benefit, endorsement, participant access or English proficiency is established. A regional introduction does not replace the chosen member organisation's decision about involvement.

sources.name: Local Contexts
sources.summary: Indigenous cultural and data-governance initiative with public support channels and guidance for community-specific labels, attribution and protocols. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: its tools are relevant when Native Nations or tourism pages need community-chosen attribution and control over cultural material.
sources.contact_route: Use the official support form or support@localcontexts.org for a focused enquiry about community-led attribution, permissions and suitable Hub resources. Note: This is a governance and technical-support route, not authority to represent a nation or permission to reuse knowledge. Decisions and agreements remain with the relevant communities.

sources.name: Engagement Institute (formerly IAP2 Australasia)
sources.summary: Participation-practitioner association with a current public contact route for membership, events and engagement resources. Suitable for feedback on P4A's civic invitation methods. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: participation practitioners can assess how a specific civic invitation can be locally shaped and presented through suitable professional channels.
sources.contact_route: Use the current contact form or info@engagementinstitute.org.au. Request routing to an appropriate practitioner discussion, event or resource contact. Note: A professional association route does not imply political endorsement, access to residents, or approval by Indigenous communities. Use the current brand and contact rather than the old IAP2 address.

sources.name: Ecotourism Australia
sources.summary: Sustainable-tourism organisation with an explicit partnership/collaboration enquiry option and a linked guide to certified operators and experiences. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: nature- and culture-based operators are a relevant audience for a locally grounded visitor-learning or community-benefit proposal.
sources.contact_route: Choose 'Partnership or collaboration' in the official enquiry form, or use eco@ecotourism.org.au. Ask which operator or professional channel is appropriate for a concise Aura Tourism proposal. Note: An enquiry does not confer certification, endorsement or permission to contact all listed operators. Any pilot, commercial arrangement and cultural content require the relevant parties' agreement.

sources.name: Independent Indigenous Tourism Operators of Queensland (IITOQ)
sources.summary: Queensland Indigenous tourism operator network whose official contact page explicitly invites partner enquiries and links a member directory. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: this is a specific operator-led route for testing whether Aura Tourism or related community interpretation is useful in a Queensland Indigenous tourism setting.
sources.contact_route: Use the official contact form or the published partner route admin@iitoq.com.au; general reception is Reception@iitoq.com.au. Request an interested operator introduction. Note: Each operator and relevant community determines cultural access, content and scope. IITOQ contact does not grant broad cultural permission or establish that the proposal is wanted.

sources.name: World Federation of Tourist Guide Associations (WFTGA)
sources.summary: Tourist-guide association network with an official association directory and regional representatives who offer public contact and referral routes. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: resident guides and guide associations offer a practical route to discussing place-based interpretation, cultural exchange and useful AI tools.
sources.contact_route: Choose a country or regional representative on the official map and use the published contact buttons. If the region is absent, write to area-reps@wftga.org for routing; consult the full-member association directory. Note: The professional network does not cover every country or culture. Membership does not establish English proficiency or authority to speak for local or Indigenous communities.

sources.name: Australian Library and Information Association — Digital Literacy Group
sources.summary: National library-sector special-interest group discussing digital technology, information verification, user education and AI, with published convenor contact links. Suggested approach: Inferred fit: this provides a precise professional audience for considering a small digital-literacy demonstration involving Verse Box, Aura or GAJRA materials.
sources.contact_route: Use the published co-convenor email links on the official group page, or ask ALIA National Office through its public Contact Us page to route a focused enquiry to the Digital Literacy Group. Note: A professional discussion does not establish a library host, approval to involve children, or access to patrons. Any activity requires the relevant library's own assessment and agreement.

sources.name: Employee Ownership Australia
sources.summary: Employee ownership association that explicitly invites conversations about projects, with co-operative resources and an expert panel. Suggested approach: Explore employee ownership and practical governance for community-scale enterprises.
sources.contact_route: Use info@employeeownership.com.au or the official contact form. Ask about worker ownership and governance for a Ready SET Co-op or community computing proposal; formal professional advice may be referred to an expert at a negotiated fee. Note: This is an initial project discussion route; professional advice may involve negotiated fees.

sources.name: Business Council of Co-operatives and Mutuals (BCCM)
sources.summary: National co-operative and mutual peak body, with a public member directory spanning sectors including care, energy, housing and education. Suggested approach: Connect community ownership and mutual benefit proposals to relevant co-operatives.
sources.contact_route: Browse the member directory to identify a relevant organisation. For a peak-body enquiry, ICA publishes info@bccm.coop as BCCM’s main organisational address. Ask who could discuss community ownership, a Ready SET Co-op or member-led care; a directory listing is not an introduction. Note: Membership and directory inclusion do not establish interest in this proposal or access to members.

sources.name: Australasian Legal Technology Alliance (ALTA)
sources.summary: Legal technology industry network supporting Australian innovation, with company and advocate participation routes. Suggested approach: Find legal technology practitioners who can discuss usable jurisdiction-specific information.
sources.contact_route: Use the official Contact us form with a short legal-information-engine demonstration and a request for a relevant practitioner or event introduction. Ask which participation route fits the project’s stage; current membership terms and any fees need checking. Note: An industry enquiry is not legal advice, legal validation or an endorsement.

sources.name: Free Access to Law Movement – member-institute discovery
sources.summary: Voluntary international association of legal-information institutes and organisations working on public access to law, described by member IALS. Suggested approach: Locate jurisdiction-specific information publishers for source and accessibility discussions.
sources.contact_route: Follow the official IALS page’s WorldLII member/declaration link to identify a jurisdiction’s legal-information institute, then verify that institute’s own organisational contact. Ask about source provenance, reuse conditions and local legal-information practice. IALS is a member, not presented here as the network secretariat. Note: Individual member contacts have not all been rechecked; data reuse and legal practice conditions remain source-specific.

sources.name: Social Enterprise Australia
sources.summary: National social enterprise peak body connecting sector development, collaboration, strategy and member networks. Suggested approach: Find suitable enterprise networks for practical community benefit and ownership proposals.
sources.contact_route: Use the official contact page or hello@socialenterpriseaustralia.org.au, published on the sector’s Understorey profile and by the Department of Social Services. Ask for the relevant local or sector network to discuss a small community enterprise proposal; funding eligibility is a separate question. Note: This is a network enquiry, not a claim of funding availability, membership acceptance or project eligibility.

sources.name: ACM SIGCHI – local and thematic chapters
sources.summary: Human–computer interaction chapter directory, with geographic groups and themes including human-centred AI, extended reality and arts in HCI. Suggested approach: Discuss accessible interaction, XR demonstrations and human-centred AI with relevant practitioners.
sources.contact_route: Use the city/country directory or relevant thematic chapter’s published contact. Ask about a short demonstration or discussion of accessible personal intelligence and XR. The directory publishes sigchi-vp-chapters@acm.org for chapter matters; check the chosen chapter’s current details before approaching it. Note: Directory availability is not willingness to host a demonstration or involve research participants.
sources.project_ids: aura-genesis aura-whole-of-life aura-child-services verse-box gajra-claude legal-engine joyful-responsible-abundance

sources.name: IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology – chapters
sources.summary: International chapter network concerned with technology’s social effects, with official local-group websites and chapter contact routes. Suggested approach: Find local conversations about community technology, responsible AI and cooperation.
sources.contact_route: Choose a local chapter website from the official list and verify its current organisational route. The page supplies ssitchaptercommittee@gmail.com for chapter coordination. Ask whether a local discussion of community data authority, responsible AI or shared benefit would fit a chapter activity. Note: The network’s geographic scope does not establish a participant or English-language access in any particular country.

sources.name: Queensland council and state international links
sources.summary: Officially documented sister-city, friendship and state relationships across 15 councils, with source evidence and responsible-team contact routes.
sources.contact_route: Choose a Queensland place and an agreement, then ask the council or state team whether an appropriate counterpart organisation could receive a relevant introduction. The register distinguishes formal sister links from other agreements and labels records needing confirmation.
